annotations.user_impact: Users may not receive live transcript text or may experience degraded results.
annotations.scope: The Omi live-transcription production service path.
annotations.verification: Verify the condition in the linked Grafana panel and correlate it with production traffic before intervention.
annotations.safe_next_action: Inspect the linked dashboard and the affected live-transcription path; mitigate through the documented service runbook only after verification.

title: Parakeet - ready pod is failing every request

model.expr: ((sum by (pod) (increase(parakeet_requests_total{container="parakeet",namespace="prod-omi-backend",status="error"}[5m])) >= 10) unless on (pod) (sum by (pod) (increase(parakeet_requests_total{container="parakeet",namespace="prod-omi-backend",status="success"}[5m])) > 0)) and on (pod) (max by (pod) (kube_pod_status_ready{namespace="prod-omi-backend",condition="true",pod=~"prod-omi-parakeet-.*"}) == 1)

annotations.summary: A Ready Parakeet pod has at least 10 failed requests and no successful requests in five minutes.
annotations.user_impact: Users routed to the affected pod are receiving transcription failures.
annotations.scope: One production Parakeet pod, evaluated independently from healthy sibling replicas.
annotations.verification: Compare per-pod success and error outcomes, then inspect the affected pod health and recent CUDA errors.
annotations.safe_next_action: If the pod is still Ready and has zero successes, replace only that replica and verify its replacement serves successful requests.

annotations.summary: A Parakeet worker detected a CUDA error that makes further inference unsafe.
annotations.user_impact: No confirmed user impact yet; the affected replica is leaving service and will be restarted automatically.
annotations.scope: One production Parakeet GPU process and its Kubernetes replica.
annotations.verification: Confirm the pod became unready, restarted, and was replaced by a replica serving successful transcription requests.
annotations.safe_next_action: Allow the health probes to recycle the replica; intervene only if the replacement also reports a fatal CUDA state.

title: Cloud Run metrics - names did not normalize

annotations.summary: Cloud Run application metrics are arriving under Stackdriver-mangled names instead of their plain omi_ names
annotations.threshold: > 0 un-normalized omi series on the cloud-run-application-metrics job for 15m
annotations.user_impact: No user impact by itself, but every alert and dashboard built on these metrics is silently matching nothing, so a real user-facing failure on a Cloud Run path could pass unnoticed.
annotations.scope: The metric_relabel_configs rewrite on the cloud-run-application-metrics scrape job.
annotations.verification: List the raw series names on that job in Grafana Explore and compare them with the rewrite regex in the kube-prometheus-stack values.
annotations.safe_next_action: Correct the rewrite regex to match the observed names and re-upgrade the monitoring release; do not add alerts against the mangled names.

title: Cloud Run metrics - egress query rejected by Cloud Monitoring

annotations.summary: The Cloud Run metrics exporter is failing its Cloud Monitoring queries, so no omi_ series are being imported
annotations.threshold: stackdriver_monitoring_last_scrape_error > 0 on the cloud-run-application-metrics job for 15m
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact, but every Cloud Run journey metric stops arriving while the exporter Deployment stays Available and its Prometheus target stays up. Panels render empty and read as no traffic rather than no ingestion, so a real user-facing failure on a Cloud Run path can run unnoticed for as long as this is firing.
annotations.scope: The dedicated Cloud Run metrics Stackdriver exporter and the Cloud Monitoring filter it is deployed with.
annotations.verification: kubectl logs the <env>-omi-cloud-run-metrics-exporter Deployment. A rejected filter logs an HTTP 400 per descriptor naming the offending expression; a missing or expired Monitoring Viewer grant on its GSA logs 403.
annotations.safe_next_action: Read the 400 back to the filter in backend/charts/monitoring/prometheus-stackdriver-exporter/<env>_omi_cloud_run_metrics_exporter.yaml, correct it, and re-run the Deploy Cloud Run Metrics Egress workflow for that environment. Cloud Monitoring rejects AND mixed with OR across resource.labels restrictions; express a disjunction as one_of(...). This egress is read-only, so nothing has to be rolled back to stop it.

title: Cloud Run metrics - egress exporter is down

annotations.summary: The Cloud Run metrics exporter is not being scraped, so no omi_ series can reach Prometheus
annotations.threshold: up < 1 on the cloud-run-application-metrics job for 15m; an absent job counts as down
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact, but every Cloud Run journey metric stops arriving. This is the case the query-rejected alert cannot see: a crashlooping or unscraped exporter publishes no error metric at all, so an error-based rule reads healthy while nothing is ingested and panels render as no traffic.
annotations.scope: The <env>-omi-cloud-run-metrics-exporter Deployment and the Prometheus job that scrapes it.
annotations.verification: kubectl get pods -n <env>-omi-monitoring for the exporter. CrashLoopBackOff with "Liveness probe failed: context deadline exceeded" means a collection is outrunning the probe or scrape budget; compare scrape_duration_seconds against the job scrape_timeout.
annotations.safe_next_action: Check whether the exporter is being killed mid-collection rather than failing: this path collects from Cloud Monitoring inline, so growth in Cloud Run series makes scrapes longer, and CPU limits or probe timeouts sized for an idle exporter will kill it once real data arrives. Raise capacity and the scrape budget in the exporter values and re-run Deploy Cloud Run Metrics Egress. Read-only egress, so nothing needs rolling back.

title: LLM Gateway - clients rejected before routing

annotations.summary: The gateway is rejecting client requests during validation, before a route is selected
annotations.user_impact: Some Omi client population is very likely failing every attempt on this path while other clients look healthy.
annotations.scope: The Omi LLM gateway request-validation path, ahead of provider routing.
annotations.verification: Confirm the rejection count in the linked panel, then split production request logs by client user agent to identify which client population is affected.
annotations.safe_next_action: Identify the rejected parameter and the client that sends it, then follow the documented gateway kill-switch runbook before changing gateway configuration.

title: LLM Gateway - lane failing a large share of real requests

annotations.summary: One gateway lane is failing more than a quarter of its real requests over an hour
annotations.threshold: failure share > 0.25 with >= 20 real requests in 1h, per lane
annotations.user_impact: The Omi capability served by this lane may be unavailable or degraded for the users who reach it.
annotations.scope: A single production LLM gateway lane; other lanes are evaluated independently.
annotations.verification: Confirm the failing lane and its provider rejection class in the linked panel before intervention.
annotations.safe_next_action: Inspect the lane route configuration and provider status on the linked dashboard, then follow the documented gateway runbook.

title: LLM Gateway - lane has served no successful request

annotations.summary: A gateway lane has made at least 20 real attempts in six hours and completed none of them
annotations.threshold: successful requests < 1 with >= 20 real attempts in 6h, per lane
annotations.user_impact: The Omi capability served by this lane is very likely completely unavailable to every user who reaches it.
annotations.scope: A single production LLM gateway lane; other lanes are evaluated independently.
annotations.verification: Confirm in the linked panel that the lane has attempts but no successful outcome, and read its provider rejection class.
annotations.safe_next_action: Inspect the lane route configuration and provider credentials on the linked dashboard, then follow the documented gateway runbook.

title: Journey outcomes - a journey stopped reporting while the platform serves traffic

model.expr: (sum by (journey) (increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{journey=~"pusher_session|capture_finalization"}[1h])) < bool 1) * on() group_left() (sum(increase(llm_gateway_requests_total[1h])) > bool 100) or (sum by (journey) (increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{journey="chat_response"}[1h])) < bool 1) * on() group_left() (sum(increase(llm_gateway_requests_total{lane_id="omi:auto:chat-agent"}[1h])) > bool 20)

annotations.summary: A journey that normally reports every hour has reported nothing while the platform is demonstrably serving traffic
annotations.threshold: 0 accepted attempts for a journey in 1h while gateway requests exceed 100 in the same hour
annotations.user_impact: Users may already be affected on this path with no other alert able to fire, because the evidence this journey's alerts depend on is missing.
annotations.scope: The real-traffic journey counters that the Omi resilience alerts are built on.
annotations.verification: Check whether the emitting service is still scraped and still running before assuming the user path itself is healthy.
annotations.safe_next_action: Restore the metrics path for the affected service first; do not treat a missing journey signal as evidence that the user path is working.

title: AI chat - agent lane traffic dropped to zero

annotations.summary: The AI chat agent lane served under 5 requests in an hour; the lowest hour in the preceding week was 18
annotations.user_impact: Users may be unable to start or continue an Omi chat at all.
annotations.scope: The Omi AI chat agent production lane.
annotations.verification: Confirm in the linked panel that request volume, not scrape availability, is what dropped.
annotations.safe_next_action: Inspect the chat entry points and gateway routing on the linked dashboard before changing configuration.

title: Firestore - NOT_FOUND read volume day-over-day step

annotations.summary: Firestore document read_count (metric stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count, type="NOT_FOUND") is running more than 2x its volume from the same hour yesterday, sustained for 2h.
annotations.threshold: avg_over_time(avg(...)[1h:1m]) > 2x the same expression offset 24h, sustained 2h
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is a cost signal, not an outage. NOT_FOUND reads are Firestore reads for documents that do not exist, so they are near-pure waste: the read is billed but returns nothing. The day-over-day comparison survives organic growth and diurnal swing, so a sustained step here is a regression rather than load.
annotations.scope: Firestore document reads across the based-hardware production project, type="NOT_FOUND" only.
annotations.verification: Compare avg_over_time(avg(stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count{type="NOT_FOUND"})[1h:1m]) against the same expression with `offset 24h`. The 2x factor is measured, not guessed: across 2026-08-18..25 excluding the incident window, normal day-over-day ratios peaked at 1.94x for a single hour, while the 2026-08-23 step held 2.4-3.4x for 24h straight. A 1.5x threshold would have false-positived on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-21. The stackdriver exporter publishes this DELTA metric as a GAUGE whose value is the per-60s-window count, so rate() is meaningless on it -- read volume must be recovered with avg_over_time(...)/60 instead. avg() (not sum()) aggregates across exporter replicas, which all report the same Cloud Monitoring series.
annotations.safe_next_action: This alert flags read volume, not cause. The Cloud Monitoring series carries module="__unknown__", so attribution needs either extending omi_firestore_read_operations_total call-site coverage or enabling a short window of Firestore DATA_READ audit logging to find the caller before making any code change.

title: Firestore - NOT_FOUND read volume above absolute ceiling

annotations.summary: Firestore document read_count (metric stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count, type="NOT_FOUND") has averaged more than 750 reads/sec over a rolling 6h window. Measured separation over 2026-08-18..25: the highest pre-incident 6h mean was 668/sec and the lowest post-incident 6h mean was 899/sec, so this threshold sits in a clean gap with ~12% margin on each side.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is a cost signal, not an outage. NOT_FOUND reads are Firestore reads for documents that do not exist, so they are near-pure waste: the read is billed but returns nothing. At the 2026-08-23 incident rate of ~950/sec this class of read alone costs roughly $740/month. This is the backstop for a leak already running at a steady elevated rate, which the day-over-day step detector cannot see because both sides of its comparison are equally elevated.
annotations.scope: Firestore document reads across the based-hardware production project, type="NOT_FOUND" only.
annotations.verification: Run avg_over_time(avg(stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count{type="NOT_FOUND"})[6h:5m]) / 60 in the linked query. Healthy 6h means run 347-668/sec; the 2026-08-23 leak holds 899-1049/sec. A 6h window is used deliberately: hourly values are extremely spiky (single healthy hours reach 1124/sec), so any shorter window false-positives. The stackdriver exporter publishes this DELTA metric as a GAUGE whose value is the per-60s-window count, so rate() is meaningless on it -- read volume must be recovered with avg_over_time(...)/60 instead. avg() (not sum()) aggregates across exporter replicas, which all report the same Cloud Monitoring series.
annotations.safe_next_action: This alert flags read volume, not cause. The Cloud Monitoring series carries module="__unknown__", so attribution needs either extending omi_firestore_read_operations_total call-site coverage or enabling a short window of Firestore DATA_READ audit logging to find the caller before making any code change.

title: Firestore - read-volume metric stopped being collected

annotations.summary: The Firestore read-volume series (stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count, type="NOT_FOUND") has been absent from Prometheus for 30m, so both Firestore cost alerts are blind.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact. This is a watchdog for the cost alerts themselves. Both Firestore cost rules are written as `expr > threshold`, which returns an empty vector when not firing; with noDataState=OK, a metric that stops arriving is indistinguishable from a healthy one. This rule is what makes that difference visible.
annotations.scope: The stackdriver-exporter series for firestore.googleapis.com/document/read_count in prod Prometheus.
annotations.verification: Query stackdriver_firestore_instance_firestore_googleapis_com_document_read_count in the linked datasource. Expect 3 series (type=LOOKUP|NOT_FOUND|QUERY). Zero series means the exporter is not publishing.
annotations.safe_next_action: This has a known cause with a known fix. Check the exporter pod for scrape errors: at monitoring.descriptor-cache-ttl=0s the exporter re-runs ListMetricDescriptors every scrape and Cloud Monitoring answers with 503 cpu-protection, which drops all series. Also check that stackdriver.metrics.interval still exceeds the ~2.4min Firestore ingestion lag -- a window shorter than the lag is always empty and yields no series at all. Both settings live in backend/charts/monitoring/prometheus-stackdriver-exporter/prod_omi_stackdriver_exporter.yaml and are applied manually per that chart README; no workflow deploys them.

title: Firestore - projected read spend per day above ceiling

annotations.summary: Projected Firestore document-read spend has exceeded $500/day on a 6h rolling mean. Measured baseline on 2026-08-25 was $344-368/day (~14,200 reads/sec), so this is ~40% headroom.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is the money rule. Unlike the NOT_FOUND rules it is shape-agnostic -- it catches a regression in LOOKUP, QUERY, or NOT_FOUND reads, from application code OR from a Firebase Extension, which the app-side probe cannot see. On 2026-08-25 QUERY reads were ~13,000/sec against NOT_FOUND ~920/sec, so a NOT_FOUND-only alert watches ~7% of the bill.
annotations.scope: All firestore.googleapis.com/document/read_count types across based-hardware production.
annotations.verification: Run the expression in the linked datasource. The $0.03/100k rate is an ASSUMPTION, not a verified Omi contract price -- re-derive from the billing export before quoting the dollar figure. The ratio and the trend are the durable signal.
annotations.safe_next_action: Break down by family with sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[1h])). On 2026-08-25 action_items_list alone was 5,079 reads/sec, ~36% of all Firestore read spend. See omi-knowledge-base/projects/gcp-cost-efficiency/candidates/C006-action-items-list-polling.md. Thresholds are measured, not guessed, and each expression was proven to return a series at a lowered threshold and nothing at its real one before shipping -- see FC-alert-never-provably-fired. stackdriver_* series are DELTA published as GAUGES (per-60s counts), so rate() on them is meaningless; omi_* _total series are real counters and rate() is correct.

title: Firestore - a read family doubled day-over-day

model.expr: (sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h])) > 2 * sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h] offset 24h))) and (sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h])) > 100)

annotations.summary: An instrumented Firestore read family is reading more than 2x the documents per second it read at the same time yesterday, and is above 100 docs/sec in absolute terms.
annotations.threshold: per-family rate > 2x the same rate offset 24h, AND > 100 docs/sec, sustained 1h
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; cost signal. This is the rule that names WHICH read path regressed -- the platform metric cannot, because all 31 firestore.googleapis.com descriptors lack any collection dimension. The 100 docs/sec floor stops small families from flapping; the 2x factor matches the measured day-over-day envelope (normal peaks reached 1.94x over 2026-08-18..25).
annotations.scope: Families instrumented via omi_firestore_read_operations_total / omi_firestore_documents_per_operation. Coverage is partial by design; a path with no family label is invisible here.
annotations.verification: sum by (family) (rate(omi_firestore_documents_per_operation_sum[2h])) against the same expression offset 24h. Baseline 2026-08-25: action_items_list 5,079/sec, listen_monthly_usage 89/sec, chat_quota_monthly_usage 13/sec.
annotations.safe_next_action: Identify the family, then find its callers. Note that "bounded" in FirestoreReadMode means a bound was applied, NOT that a cache exists -- action_items_list is bounded at limit=500 and still reads ~5,000 docs/sec because every client poll re-reads the list. Thresholds are measured, not guessed, and each expression was proven to return a series at a lowered threshold and nothing at its real one before shipping -- see FC-alert-never-provably-fired. stackdriver_* series are DELTA published as GAUGES (per-60s counts), so rate() on them is meaningless; omi_* _total series are real counters and rate() is correct.

annotations.summary: The Firestore read-volume series is still present but has not been updated in over 15 minutes, so the cost alerts are running on frozen data.
annotations.user_impact: No direct user impact; this is a watchdog for the cost alerts. It is the companion to omi-firestore-metric-absent: absent() catches a series that vanished, this catches a series that is present but wedged. Every other cost rule here is written as `expr > threshold`, which returns empty when not firing, and with noDataState=OK a frozen or missing metric is indistinguishable from a healthy one.
annotations.scope: The stackdriver-exporter series for firestore.googleapis.com/document/read_count in prod Prometheus.
annotations.verification: time() - max(timestamp(...)) -- healthy is under ~240s given the exporter scrape interval plus the ~2.4min Cloud Monitoring sample lag. Measured 134-143s on 2026-08-25.
annotations.safe_next_action: Check the exporter pod for scrape errors and 503 cpu-protection throttling, and confirm stackdriver.metrics.interval still exceeds the Firestore ingestion lag. Both settings live in backend/charts/monitoring/prometheus-stackdriver-exporter/prod_omi_stackdriver_exporter.yaml and are applied MANUALLY per that chart README -- no workflow deploys them. Thresholds are measured, not guessed, and each expression was proven to return a series at a lowered threshold and nothing at its real one before shipping -- see FC-alert-never-provably-fired. stackdriver_* series are DELTA published as GAUGES (per-60s counts), so rate() on them is meaningless; omi_* _total series are real counters and rate() is correct.

title: Capture finalization - canonical memory admission failure

annotations.summary: A real capture finalization was rejected by the canonical-memory runtime admission fence
annotations.threshold: at least one memory_fence or memory_config finalization failure in 5m
annotations.user_impact: At least one accepted voice capture could not complete finalization because its serving runtime could not safely mutate canonical memory.
annotations.scope: Persisted conversation finalization on Pusher and Cloud Tasks workers.
annotations.verification: Confirm the bounded reason and exact serving image/config receipt; do not infer the cause from HTTP status or workflow state alone.
annotations.safe_next_action: Halt promotion, preserve the durable retry queue, and restore a capability-admitted image plus config bundle before replay.

title: Capture finalization - success rate below paging floor

annotations.summary: Capture finalization success share below the 90% paging floor while at least 20 journeys were accepted in 30m
annotations.user_impact: Voice recordings are accepted but not becoming conversations; users lose captures entirely.
annotations.scope: The capture-finalization journey outcome on backend-listen.
annotations.verification: Confirm the success tile and the accepted-vs-settled panel on the linked Core Features dashboard before intervention.
annotations.safe_next_action: Follow the real-traffic journeys runbook; treat a low success share with real accepted traffic as a user-facing outage, not a capacity signal.

title: Capture finalization - accepted work is not settling

annotations.summary: At least 100 capture journeys were accepted in 1h while more than 50 of them per hour never reached any terminal outcome
annotations.threshold: accepted >= 100 per 1h and accepted - settled > 50 per 1h
annotations.user_impact: Captures are queueing without outcomes; the finalization backlog grows and users do not get their conversations.
annotations.scope: The capture-finalization accept and terminal counters on backend-listen.
annotations.verification: Confirm the accepted-vs-settled gap and the oldest unfinished job on the linked Core Features dashboard before intervention.
annotations.safe_next_action: Follow the real-traffic journeys runbook; inspect finalization worker health and the Firestore job queue before any pod restarts.

title: Capture finalization - oldest unfinished job too old

annotations.summary: The oldest unfinished capture finalization job has been waiting longer than 1 hour
annotations.user_impact: At least one user capture has been stuck for over an hour; sustained backlogs mean many users are missing conversations.
annotations.scope: The finalization job queue age gauge republished by backend-listen.
annotations.verification: Confirm the oldest unfinished job tile and the unfinished-jobs panel on the linked Core Features dashboard before intervention.
annotations.safe_next_action: Follow the real-traffic journeys runbook; the gauge aggregates with max across listener pods, so verify one pod is not reporting a stale value.

annotations.summary: More than 50 capture finalization jobs were terminalized as dead letters in 1h
annotations.user_impact: Each dead letter is a user capture that failed every retry and will never become a conversation.
annotations.scope: The finalization dead-letter counter on backend-listen.
annotations.verification: Confirm the dead-letter tile and the retries panel on the linked Core Features dashboard before intervention.
annotations.safe_next_action: Follow the real-traffic journeys runbook; dead letters after a backlog often point at the finalization worker, not the listener.

model.queryText: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND (textPayload:"STARTUP TCP probe failed" OR textPayload:"instance could not start successfully")

annotations.safe_next_action: Do not deploy a new Cloud Run revision (starts will fail). Check GCP status for us-central1. Wait for instance starts to succeed.
annotations.scope: Cloud Run revisions in based-hardware matching STARTUP TCP probe failed or instance could not start successfully.
annotations.summary: Cloud Run instances are failing to start (STARTUP TCP probe / instance could not start).
annotations.user_impact: New requests queue or hang while warm minScale instances can still return /health 200. This is the 2026-09-01 us-central1 failure mode.
annotations.verification: Cloud Logging: resource.type=cloud_run_revision AND textPayload:STARTUP TCP probe failed. Contrast api.omi.me vs a warm instance.

title: Chat-first proactive delivery - ready queue stalled

annotations.summary: A Chat-first proactive queue with an intent older than 24 hours was fetched during the last hour
annotations.threshold: non-zero stalled event rate over 1h for 5m
annotations.user_impact: Meeting notes and daily opener cards may be delayed behind an intent that is not reaching a terminal state.
annotations.scope: The account-scoped Chat-first proactive fetch and acknowledgement path.
annotations.verification: Break down chat_first_proactive_total by source and reason, then compare fetch, rejected, reconciled, and dead-letter events.
annotations.safe_next_action: Inspect recent backend and desktop kernel errors; verify poison intents are reaching reconciled or dead-letter state before changing any retry budget.

title: Durable queue - oldest ready item stalled

annotations.summary: A durable queue has a ready item older than 6 hours, or the omi_queue_oldest_ready_age_seconds gauge is absent
annotations.threshold: oldest ready age > 6h or absent() for 5m
annotations.user_impact: Independent items behind a poison head can stall: memories, task integrations, Chat-first cards, or capture finalization may stop advancing.
annotations.scope: Every backend durable queue that publishes omi_queue_oldest_ready_age_seconds.
annotations.verification: Break down omi_queue_oldest_ready_age_seconds by queue, then inspect that queue's dead-letter rows and last_error_text before changing retry budgets.
annotations.safe_next_action: Confirm poison items reached a dead letter; redrive by identity only after the error is understood. Do not raise the attempt budget.
